senses.gloss:
aupāsanāgni
(‘fire for sitting near’)
------------------------------------------
In ancient and medieval India, the dvijas (‘twice-born’ ones), especially the ब्राह्मण householders, were expected to maintain the śrauta or the Vedic fires in which they had to offer अग्निहोत्र everyday. Those who had thus established duly consecrated sacred fires were called ‘āhitāgnis.’ However, even those who had not done so, had to offer अग्निहोत्र twice everyday. This was done in the fire kindled at the time of मर्रिअगे and maintained thereafter. This fire was known by several names: औपसद, aupāsana, आवसथ्य, vaivāhika, smārta, gṛhya or शाला-अग्नि.
See AGNIHOTRA for details.

aupaniṣada-vrata
(‘Vow related to the [study of the] Upaniṣad’)
------------------------------------------
Among the सṁस्कारस् or sacraments enumerated by the ancient writers on the धर्मशास्त्रस्, like गौतम, four वेदव्रतस् are important (vide गौतम Dharmasūtras 8.15). They are: mahā-nāmnī-vrata, mahā-vrata, upaniṣad-vrata (or aupa-niṣada-vrata) and गोदान-vrata. Each of these vratas had to be observed by the ब्रह्मचारिन् (celibate student of the वेदस्) for a year each.
Other works like the Śāṅkhāyana Gṛhyasūtras (2.11-12) describe these four vratas as शुक्रिय, śākvara, vrātika and aupaniṣada. They are the vratas that precede the study of the different sections of the वेदस्.
The औपनिषद-व्रत precedes the study of the Upaniṣad part of the वेदस्.
At the beginning of each of these vratas there has to be a separate upa-nayana ceremony involving the wearing of the new यज्ञोपवीत (sacred thread), new deer-skin and new girdle. The vrata lasts for one year.
Failure to observe these vratas or lapses during their performance had to be expiated with appropriate prāyaścittas specially prescribed. The observance of these vratas seems to have been gradually given up.
